4. Learned counsel for the deponents submits that the controversy involved in the case related to the income certificate dated 6.12.2018 produced by the applicant no. 1 in proceedings under Section 12 of the Domestic Violence Act.
Sri Prakhar Tandon, learned counsel for the deponents submits that they have filed the affidavit on the basis of the records available before the trial court.
Who had filed the affidavit along with the alleged forged income certificate dated 6.12.2018 in proceedings under Section 12 of the Domestic Violence Act, is not in the knowledge of the deponents.
5. Learned counsel for applicants no. 1, 2 and 4 is not present before the Court.

Though Sri Prakhar Tandon submits that he has instructions to appear on behalf of all the applicants but no vakalatnama has been filed on their behalf.
6.

The allegation in the instant complaint case filed by the opposite party no. 2 against the applicants revolves around the forged income certificate dated 6.12.2018 filed in the proceedings under the Domestic Violence Act before the trial court, which requires a detailed factual examination and is possible during the trial of the case.

The factual examination of the said document, how the same was issued and who obtained the same and how the same was filed in proceedings under Section 12 of the Domestic Violence Act, is a matter of fact which can be examined only during the trial of the case.
The trial court on the basis of material available on record has found a prima facie case against the applicants.
Thus, this Court do not find any good reason to entertain the instant application.
7. In view of the aforesaid, the instant application stands dismissed.
8. Personal appearance of deponents-Rajesh Baboo Mishra and Rajeev Kumar is exempted.
